plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub or small tree with glossy dark green leaves and showy rose-like flowers. It is widely cultivated in temperate gardens and thrives in partial shade with acidic, well-drained soil.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (December to April in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea and China; cultivated in the southeastern United States, Europe and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is closely related to Camellia sinensis, the plant used to make tea, and camellia oil has been used in Japan for centuries as a hair and skin treatment.

plants.name: Hippeastrum puniceum
plants.description: A bulbous perennial producing large trumpet-shaped flowers on tall hollow stalks. In the wild it grows in tropical and subtropical regions, and hybrids are popular as potted plants and in warm gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter in the Northern Hemisphere when forced indoors; wild and garden plants bloom in the Southern Hemisphere summer (December to February)
plants.location: Native to Central and South America and the Caribbean; grown worldwide
plants.funFact: Many plants sold as amaryllis are actually Hippeastrum, a different genus from the true South African Amaryllis belladonna.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: A clump-forming perennial with strap-like leaves and rounded umbels of tubular blue flowers held on tall stalks. It is tolerant of heat and drought and is common in coastal gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere (December to February)
plants.location: Native to South Africa; widely naturalized in Australia and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Despite its common name, Agapanthus is not a true lily. Its name comes from the Greek words for 'love' and 'flower'.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: A low evergreen perennial that blooms during the coldest months, with nodding saucer-shaped white flowers surrounding golden stamens. It thrives in woodland conditions with alkaline soil.
plants.bloomingSeason: Midwinter to early spring (December to March)
plants.location: Native to the mountains of central and southern Europe; cultivated in temperate gardens
plants.funFact: Despite blooming in snow, hellebores are poisonous, and in folklore they were once believed to ward off evil spirits.
